passages.locator: President of the Indian National Congress
passages.excerpt_preview: ubhas Chandra Bose was President of the Indian National Congress in 1938–1939 and raised and led the Indian National Army against Allied forces during the Second World War.
Gandhi judged his patriotism second to none, but Bose’s actions generated controversy in India and condemnation in the West.
The biography treats his public and private life as revealing contradictions in the world history of the first half of the twentieth century.
